pages.text: $(l)Oil deposits$()$(br)In every Overworld biome, roughly one chunk in sixteen hides an oil field on the $(item)bedrock floor, at Y -64$(). It is made of one or more $(item)oil deposit$() blocks a few blocks apart. Above each deposit rises a column of $(item)crude oil$() up to 24 blocks high, with $(item)fossilstone$() beside its lower part.

$(li)An oil deposit cannot be mined, blown up or moved, and never drops anything. It stays where it is and you pump it with a pumpjack.$(li)Each deposit holds a random reserve, between 1000 and the server's maximum (10000 by default).
$(li)Fossilstone is twice as hard as obsidian: mine it with a pickaxe and patience.

$(l)Oil wells$()$(br)In biomes that can hold a desert pyramid, about one chunk in 500 has an $(item)oil well$(): an oil deposit with a column of crude oil climbing from bedrock to about $(item)70 blocks above the surface$(). You cannot miss it.
The oil hammer and the surface scanner, which find deposits for you, need steel: they are covered in the oil chapter.
